summary: Orphaned NVMe partitions after USB-C dock hot-swap during depot repair causing imaging and BitLocker failures
description: Issue summary: Several depot repair tickets from the last week report machines that fail imaging or drop into BitLocker recovery after a routine USB-C dock disconnect and hot-swap while NVMe is present. Impact: Machines returned to users with missing OS boot entries or BitLocker recovery prompts; blocks re-provisioning pipeline for affected units. Environment: Depot repair bench (staging-us-west), Windows 11 22H2 imaging profile, latest vendor NVMe drivers deployed via driverstore. Initial discovery: Repair tech unplugged a USB-C dock while NVMe drive remained active (hot-swap). After reconnect and power cycle, device shows additional orphaned EFI partitions or changed disk GUIDs so imaging fails to attach expected OS volumes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Boot machine from WinPE recovery media with NVMe mounted and a USB-C dock connected (external USB hub present)
2) While OS image still assigned (WinPE session or Windows running in lab), unplug USB-C dock without performing safe removal for hub-attached devices
3) Reconnect dock and perform standard reboot to Windows PE imaging target
4) Run imaging task (image-builder v4.3) and notice imaging script cannot locate expected disk by signature; Diskpart lists unexpected extra EFI partition and missing OS partition
5) Attempt to continue results in BitLocker recovery or imaging abort with code 0x80070057 or 'no match for disk signature'.
logs: 2026-03-07 14:12:23 WinPE image-builder: ERROR ImageTask: failed to find disk with signature 0x3B2A1C4D - found disks: 0x9F1E2D3C, 0x3B2A1C4D (offline)

2026-03-07 14:12:26 diskpart: Disk ### Status Size Free Dyn Gpt
  Disk 0 Online 476 GB 0 B *
  Disk 1 Offline 512 GB 0 B *
2026-03-07 14:13:02 kernel: nvme0n1: controller reset due to sudden detach (dmesg capture from lab image log)
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: USB-C dock hot-swap leaves NVMe controller in a transient state where the device returns with new GUIDs or exposes hidden recovery partition first.
Hypothesis 2: Vendor NVMe driver or firmware on certain SKUs does not gracefully handle bus detach/reattach under Windows PE, causing driverstore to register a duplicate device instance path.
Reproduced: Lab tech reproduced on Dell-Precision-5560 with dock model PD-2100 following steps above; observed orphaned EFI partition and disk signature mismatch.

Checked imaging logs and image-builder code: imaging looks up disk by signature GUID; when signature changes imaging treats disk as foreign and fails fast rather than performing fallback by model/size.
Driver/firmware correlation: Both affected units have NVMe firmware v1.2.3 and vendor-provided Windows driver 2.1.0 deployed. A Lenovo unit with newer firmware v1.3.0 did not reproduce the issue.

Temporary mitigation tested: Running 'diskpart -s cleanup-and-reassign.cmd' to clear orphan partitions and reapply expected GPT data let imaging succeed, but this is destructive and requires tech confirmation and data wipe — acceptable in depot but dangerous if done incorrectly.
Related past ticket: INT-31842 had an NVMe behavior after imaging referenced as similar symptom; cross-checked but root cause differs (that ticket was driverstore DKMS conflict in Ubuntu imaging).

suggested_workaround: On depot bench, instruct techs to fully power down the machine before unplugging docks during repair workflows. Use provided depot cleanup script (disk-wipe-and-gpt-restore.ps1) to remove orphan partitions and rebuild GPT before imaging. Do not run cleanup on user-returned devices without explicit user data wipe authorization.
resolution: Open - vendor firmware validation in-progress. Imaging fallback patch created and awaiting SRE deploy to staging imaging fleet.
resolution_notes: Patch adds a size+model match fallback when disk signature lookup fails, reducing false negatives in imaging. Firmware team engaged with NVMe vendor for a definitive firmware fix. Post-deploy we will run a 48-hour soak test in lab with dock hot-swap cycles. Follow-up ticket will track vendor firmware rollout to affected SKUs.
